question.problem:
Find the point(s) of the intersection of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+3{z}^{2}=1$ and the line 
$\{\begin{aligned}x=-t \\ y=t, \\ z=t\end{aligned}$ where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
question.worked_solution:
Substituting the expressions for $x$, $y$, and $z$ from the parametric equation of the line into the equation of the ellipsoid, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}+3{z}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+6{z}^{2} & =2 \\ (-t)^{2}+2(t)^{2}+6(t)^{2} & =2 \\ {t}^{2}+2{t}^{2}+6{t}^{2} & =2 \\ 9{t}^{2} & =2 \\ {t}^{2} & =\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $t=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ and $t=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}.$ 

Now, we substitute our solutions back into the equations of the line.

- For $t=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ y=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ z=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

so the first point is $(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}).$

- For $t=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ y=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\ z=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

so the second point is $(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})$ and $(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}).$
